name: HYLU
language: C (C API header with extern "C", closed-source prebuilt library)
workload: Parallel sparse LU solve (preprocessing, numerical factorization, forward-backward substitution) of 37 SuiteSparse Matrix Collection matrices with dimensions 525,825 to 5,558,326, wall time with 16 threads.
claimed_speedup: One-time solve: 1.70X faster than Intel MKL PARDISO on geometric mean in total time (preprocessing + factorization + solve); 2.36X faster in numerical factorization, 1.48X faster in preprocessing, but forward-backward substitution 18% slower. Repeated solve with identical sparsity pattern: 2.90X faster in numerical factorization, 2.53X faster in factorization + solve total, forward-backward substitution 20% slower. Also claims an order of magnitude higher accuracy (residual) on geometric mean.
compiler_and_flags: Test code compiled with gcc 13.3.0 (flags not stated); HYLU library compiled with gcc 8.5.0 on Rocky Linux 8.10 (flags not stated); MKL 2025.3; HYLU version 20260331
hardware: Intel Xeon Gold 6130 @ 2.1GHz, 256GB memory, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, 16 threads
tradeoffs: Closed source: the repo ships one C header (include/) plus prebuilt x64 libraries (centos7_x64_mkl, centos7_x64_openblas, win7_x64_mkl, win7_x64_openblas) and a demo; no solver source. Needs an x64 CPU with AVX2 and FMA; Windows or Linux only (README names Windows 7/10/11 and CentOS 7/8, other mainstream Linux said to work). Supports unsymmetric, symmetric indefinite and symmetric positive-definite matrices, real and complex, 32-bit and 64-bit index APIs. Forward-backward substitution is slower than MKL PARDISO (18-20% on geometric mean), so the win comes from preprocessing and factorization.
caveats: First-party evidence only: README and doc/results.pdf by the author, plus the author's arXiv preprint 2509.07690 (not opened; arXiv is unreachable from this environment). Benchmark code is not public (only demo/ is in the repo), and compiler flags are not stated, so this cannot be Tier A. No license file or license statement was found in the repo listing or README, and only binaries are provided, so the code cannot be copied or reimplemented from source; usability is reference and has_code is false (no source). Baseline is Intel MKL PARDISO, not SuiteSparse, Eigen sparse or PETSc, so there is no direct comparison against the category baselines. The matrix set is limited to 37 large SuiteSparse matrices (n >= 525,825), and the results.pdf was produced with HYLU version 20260331 while the README's latest version is 20260930. Repo history runs from 2025-09-12 (initial release) to 2026-09-30. The README quotes 1.70X (total, one-time) and 2.53X (repeated, factorization + solve); results.pdf additionally gives the 2.36X and 2.90X numerical-factorization figures. A sibling project by the same author, CKTSO, is already catalogued (https://github.com/chenxm1986/cktso).
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch 'Show HN sparse Cholesky LU solver faster than SuiteSparse' with allowed_domains news.ycombinator.com returned the arXiv paper HYLU 2509.07690, not an HN thread; no Hacker News thread about HYLU was found. A follow-up WebSearch 'HYLU hybrid parallel sparse LU factorization github' led to the repo.
